RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

The all-male panel is, on its own, weak evidence. It's common in economics departments and reflects the field's demographics more than any individual decision. Panels like this can produce fair outcomes, and mixed panels can produce unfair ones.

Your stronger facts are concrete: a completed PhD versus an unfinished one, six papers versus two, four years of teaching — and two weeks of silence on a written explanation you're likely entitled to.

So lead with the substance. Pursue the written reasons, in writing, citing any statutory or institutional deadline. Mention panel composition only as context if the explanation turns out to be thin or shifting, not as your opening argument. It's a question mark, not a finding.
